subject: Onramp: benchmark intake + ops matrix for SLOs
messages:
From: Tom Reddington <tom@acme-corp.com>
To: ava_chen <ava@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finserv.io>
Date: 2026-11-17T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Onramp: initial discovery notes

Thanks for the call this morning, Ava — quick follow-up with our priorities so we have a single source of truth for the benchmark work.

Top objectives for Acme: 
- Latency target: 95th percentile < 120ms for short prompt path (<= 256 tokens).
- Bulk inference throughput for batch scoring: sustained 2500 requests/minute during nightly runs.
- Concurrent streaming: up to 120 concurrent streaming connections with real-time partial outputs (stream fragment cadence ~100-200ms).
- Determinism: results should be reproducible across runs within prompt set V1; we will accept small top-k variability but require stable latency profiles.

We attached an initial spreadsheet with sample prompt buckets; please review and propose an ops matrix (who owns what, what data to collect, measurement hooks). Priya — looping you for compliance notes (audit logs, retention).

Next steps from our side: we can provision a sandbox dataset and agree to two checkpoints: (1) measurement-spec signoff (this week), (2) first run and readout (next week).

Tom
Senior ML Engineer
Acme Corp

Attachments: acme_benchmark_intake_v0.3.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: ava_chen <ava@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reddington <tom@acme-corp.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-17T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Onramp: initial discovery notes

Tom — thanks, this is clear and helpful. I pulled the intake sheet into the shared drive and added two tabs: 'measurement-spec' and 'ops-matrix'.

Quick clarifications before we draft the formal measurement-spec: 
1) Latency baseline: is the 120ms 95th target measured on your client side (post-network) or server-side (Redwood edge)? If client, please share geo distribution.
2) For batch scoring: confirm payload size distribution (avg tokens per request) and whether the nightly run can be queued (we can schedule burst capacity).
3) Streaming cadence: do you require per-token flush or batched fragments (we recommend 100ms fragmenting by default to stay within connection limits).

Proposed owners in ops-matrix:
- Redwood measurement-spec author: Ava Chen (draft)
- Redwood benchmark runner: Marcus Lin (execution + logs capture)
- Acme dataset & prompt steward: Tom Reddington
- Compliance liaison: Priya Shah (audit/retention)

I'll draft a concise measurement-spec and share today; Marcus will evaluate expected GPU profile and give cost/throughput trade-offs in the run plan.

Ava Chen
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Related link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AqBenchmarkOnramp

From: marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: ava_chen <ava@redwood.ai>, Tom Reddington <tom@acme-corp.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T08:47:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Onramp: initial discovery notes

Tom/Ava — quick technical note after a first pass on the prompt buckets (thanks for the sheet). Two immediate items that will affect throughput/latency: 

1) Token distribution: the "short" bucket has a nontrivial tail (some requests spike to ~600 tokens). If those are frequent (>=5%), we should split them into a separate "mid" bucket. 600-token requests change kernel selection and KV cache sizing; 95th will jump unless we route them to a different instance class.

2) Streaming mode: our streaming soft-SLOs assume 80 concurrent streams on a single A100-equivalent instance with optimized batching. 120 concurrent streams is feasible but will require either (a) dedicated pool sizing (recommended) or (b) per-customer connection throttling during peak.

I'll attach a short run-plan stub (linked in drive) showing expected p95 projection across instance tiers and a suggested run configuration for the first benchmark (2-hour ramp with three steady-state windows).

Marcus Lin
Benchmarking Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment referenced: streaming_requirements_notes.pdf

From: Tom Reddington <tom@acme-corp.com>
To: marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, ava_chen <ava@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finserv.io>
Date: 2026-11-18T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Onramp: initial discovery notes

Appreciate the quick analysis, Marcus. A few answers from our side: 
- Token tail: confirmed ~7% are >512 tokens due to verbose product descriptions. We can tag those into a separate prompt stream.
- Streaming: 120 concurrent is a hard SLO for our real-time feature — we need guidance on cost estimates for a dedicated pool. Also need to confirm whether Redwood's prefix caching will help for repeated session continuations.

Can you include estimated cost delta between shared vs dedicated pool in the run-plan? We'll need that for procurement signoff.

Tom

On attachments: I uploaded a small sample set to the drive folder for the benchmark run.

From: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reddington <tom@acme-corp.com>, ava_chen <ava@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-19T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Onramp: initial discovery notes — action items and timeline

Thanks everyone — summarizing agreed next steps and owners (ops-matrix row format):

1) Measurement-spec draft (deadline: 2026-11-18 EOD) — Owner: Ava Chen — includes precise p50/p95/p99 definitions, client vs server measurement points, and seed set for reproducibility.
2) Run-plan + cost delta (deadline: 2026-11-19 noon) — Owner: Marcus Lin — includes per-tier p95 projections and dedicated pool vs shared pool cost delta.
3) Sample artifacts & prompt tagging (deadline: 2026-11-19 EOD) — Owner: Tom Reddington — upload sample prompts and label >512 token examples.
4) Compliance checklist (deadline: 2026-11-20) — Owner: Priya Shah — audit retention, encryption, and access control notes.
5) First benchmark run (tentative): 2026-11-23 — Redwood executes 2-hour ramp and shares logs + artifacts.

I've attached a one-page ops-matrix snapshot to the drive and left comments on the intake sheet. If there are no objections, we'll convert the measurement-spec draft into a signed checklist and move to scheduling.

Kimberly Park
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: ops-matrix snapshot (drive link), measurement-spec draft (drive link)
